residents.name: Marisol Fernwick
residents.capabilities: Grows herb beds and tea plants on the farm tower terrace and blends the teas the night market pours for anyone who walks by.
residents.limitations: Knows plants and teas only; leaves cranes, steel and glass to the site crew and wiring to the fabricators.
barks: The mint on level nine is ready tonight. A leaf in cold water makes a long shift feel easy.
Come by the night market for a cup of chamomile. Takes about two minutes and the tea is free.
Rooftop basil likes the glow from the magenta signs, which is a funny thing to learn at midnight.
I wear my gloves and my hoodie in the grow rooms. The plants are cool, the people are cooler.
If you pass level nine, take a sprig of rosemary. There is always more than we need.
Good compost smells like rain on warm pavement. That is how I know the trays are happy.

residents.name: Kwame Oakhand
residents.capabilities: Runs the grain and rice trays in the hydroponic racks and watches the humidity in the seed bank so every variety stays ready to plant.
residents.limitations: Looks after crops and seeds only; asks the site crew for anything involving structure and the researchers for data.
barks: Rice trays in the third rack are green already. Come up and see, the lights make it look like a small lake.
The seed bank is kept cool and dry. I check the dials twice, because seeds cannot tell us when they are cold.
Rotating the grain trays is like timetabling a tram line. Each one has a turn and none waits too long.
I learned most of this from the research tower notes. Ask a researcher if I get a number wrong.
Seeds from three continents sit in that vault, and every jar has a hand-written label.
A pot of rice and a window with a view of the avenue. That is my favourite way to end a shift.

residents.name: Ludmila Greenfield
residents.capabilities: Grows fibre crops such as flax, hemp and nettle in the sky rows, and sends the harvest to the fabricators for cloth and bio-composite panels.
residents.limitations: Grows and harvests fibre only; spinning, printing and weaving belong to the fabricators.
barks: Flax looks like a pale blue haze on the roof. Come at sunrise, before the avenue wakes up.
Nettle makes a surprisingly soft cloth. The fabricators will show you a scarf if you ask nicely.
Hemp stalks go to the workshop hall for panels. Nothing leaves my rows without a plan for it.
I carry a thermos of tea from the night market. The sky rows are windy even in summer.
These plants clean the air a little, and the lab says so. I like having proof.
If you are heading to the library, say hello to the flax on level twelve. It likes company.

residents.name: Bao Rainwell
residents.capabilities: Designs the rain-capture tanks and drip lines of the farm tower so every root gets water without waste.
residents.limitations: Plans water only; asks the site crew to lift tanks into place and the researchers to confirm flow numbers.
barks: The tanks on the roof fill from the evening mist. By morning the whole tower has a drink.
Drip lines are like transit lines for water. If one stops, the whole row feels it.
I clean the filters every Thursday. Tidy filters mean clear water for the noodle stall.
A gentle slope on the roof is all it takes. Water is very patient, you only need to show it the way.
Come see the cistern under the guesthouse. It is bigger than it looks and very quiet.
I always check the sensors with a friend. Two sets of eyes beat one, even on a calm night.

residents.name: Saoirse Meadowlark
residents.capabilities: Raises root crops in stacked cold trays under the market and keeps the cold-chain vaults tidy for the night market kitchens.
residents.limitations: Grows and stores roots only; leaves the stalls to the hosts and fabricators and building work to the site crew.
barks: Carrots in the cold vault taste sweeter after a few days in the dark. Funny how patience does that.
The vault door is heavy but friendly. Push gently and it glides.
Parsnips do well downstairs, away from the neon. They like the quiet, I think.
Taking a break under the amphitheatre lights helps me think. Join me if the stairs are not too busy.
Every crate has a date and a name. That way nothing waits too long and nothing is wasted.
Cold hands, warm heart, my gran used to say. I wear fingerless gloves and drink lots of tea.

residents.name: Tobiah Thistle
residents.capabilities: Tends the dwarf fruit trees on the roof terraces, grafting pear, plum and apple so the night market always has fruit to share.
residents.limitations: Grows fruit trees only; asks the site crew about railings and the researchers about pollinator counts.
barks: Plums on terrace four are nearly ripe. I will leave a basket by the lift for anyone who wants one.
A graft takes patience. You tie it, you wait, and one spring a new branch says hello.
These trees grow in planter boxes, but their roots still reach down for water. They are hopeful like that.
I wear a cap and a reflective vest on the roof so the maintenance drones know where I am.
Fruit stall is open at market hour. Take two pears and tell me which one you liked better.
My favourite sound in Harr is bees on blossom with the tram humming far below.

residents.name: Ignatius Stonebrook
residents.capabilities: Cuts and sets composite foundation blocks and levels plinths for towers, sky bridge piers and plaza paving.
residents.limitations: Builds foundations only; asks the researchers for load numbers and the fabricators for custom fittings.
barks: Every tower sits on a level plinth. Skip that step and the whole skyline leans.
I measure the base twice, wearing my hard hat and my favourite jacket. Twice is a good habit.
Come stand at the observatory site. A crew of two or more is all it takes to place the next stage.
Composite blocks are light for their strength. Two people can set one if they count together.
Sky walk piers go in tomorrow. Bring a friend if you want to watch and lend a hand.
At the end of the shift I like to sit on the finished plinth and look at the lights.

residents.name: Fenwick Ashcombe
residents.capabilities: Frames curved steel-and-glass arches and canopies, and assembles sky bridge sections from prefabricated parts.
residents.limitations: Frames and fits only; relies on the researchers for stress data and on the foundation crew for the base.
barks: That arch over the transit hub took four of us and a very patient crane operator.
Curved glass looks delicate but carries a lot. A small lesson in how shape matters.
I coil my cables the same way every time. It saves time and nobody trips.
Look up at the sky walk. Each section was lifted at dusk when the wind eased.
Between lifts I stretch on the lawn near the festival lights. Join me, it helps the back.
I started as a window cleaner. Now I put the windows up. Not a bad change.

residents.name: Casimir Lathe
residents.capabilities: Fits precision joints, rails and lift tracks so elevators, trams and sliding doors run quietly and safely.
residents.limitations: Works on rails and fittings only; leaves frames to the framers and software to the researchers.
barks: A good rail is a straight line that never complains. I like quiet machines.
Elevator guides need oil and care. Ten minutes a week keeps them silent for years.
The glass garden doors slide so smoothly you forget they are there. That is the compliment I want.
Hold the handrail on the long stairs. The paint is dry now and the neon strip is a good guide.
Come to the water tower site if you like gears. The valve wheel is satisfying to turn.
At night I listen to the trams from my balcony. When they hum evenly, I sleep well.

residents.name: Hollis Quarrier
residents.capabilities: Selects recycled aggregate, tests load-bearing blocks and finishes the walls and paving of the lower avenues.
residents.limitations: Tests and finishes masonry only; asks the researchers for lab reports and the site crew for placement.
barks: Crushed old pavement becomes the base of the new one. Nothing goes to waste in Harr.
A test block should hum, not crack. I press every sample and write down what I hear.
The pavilion floor has a faint pink tint from recycled glass. Look closely in the lamplight.
My boots are well worn and my notebook is full. Come ask me anything about pavement.
I sit in the glass garden when my back aches. The warm air helps and the plants do not mind.
The water tower base is finished. Walk around it and listen to the echo.

residents.name: Pelham Wrightson
residents.capabilities: Assembles modular frames, scaffold stages and raised platforms for towers, schools and solar fields.
residents.limitations: Builds frames and stages only; defers to the researchers on safety limits and to the fabricators on special parts.
barks: A scaffold is like a ladder with good manners. Everyone gets a turn and nobody pushes.
The schoolhouse frame went up in a day with eight pairs of hands. It felt like a dance.
The second solar field needs more panel rails. We start when the crew count reaches two.
I label every bolt with a tiny coloured sticker. My niece suggested pink and cyan, and it works.
Annex site has the best view of the east lamps. Come at dusk and bring tea.
Safety harness check, then the tea break. In that order, always.

residents.name: Imara Bakewell
residents.capabilities: Cooks the noodles, steamed buns and sweet bean pastries at the night market stalls and teaches anyone who asks.
residents.limitations: Cooks and serves only; leaves farming to the growers and building to the site crew. Always checks with the hosts about the stall schedule.
barks: Noodles at the plaza stall, hot and free. Bring your own appetite and a friend.
My apron has more steam stains than a sky train window. I wear them proudly.
Sweet bean buns rise best when the kitchen is warm and the radio is playing something gentle.
If the line is long, enjoy the neon. It changes colour every few minutes.
I learned the dough from a neighbour on level six. Now I teach it to whoever stands still long enough.
No one leaves the night market hungry. That is the one rule I never bend.

residents.name: Yuki Pottersby
residents.capabilities: Prints and fires ceramic bowls, cups and planters for the night market and the farm terraces.
residents.limitations: Makes ceramics only; gets clay offcuts from the fabrication alley and asks the growers what planters they need.
barks: Each bowl is printed in layers, then fired. The pattern is a little different every time.
Hold a warm bowl with both hands. It is the oldest kind of hello, even on a rooftop.
The noodle stall's bowls came out of my oven this morning. Please bring them back after the meal.
I wear a canvas apron and trainers. Clay on the floor is part of the job and the city forgives it.
A planter that fits its plant makes everything easier. Tell me what you grow and I will print one.
Slow work calms me. The printer hums, the glaze glows, and the wind blows over the wind array.

residents.name: Zuri Loomsworth
residents.capabilities: Weaves and sews rain capes, soft blankets and reflective jackets from recycled fibres for the farm rows and the avenues.
residents.limitations: Makes textiles only; leaves fastenings to the fabrication labs and fibre growing to the growers.
barks: A light rain cape folds smaller than a sandwich. Try one on if the mist comes in.
The reflective stripes catch the neon beautifully. They keep the sky walk runners easy to spot.
Soft blankets are for the guesthouse, but the bench by the orchard gate gets one in cold weather.
I thread every needle by hand, even though the machine is faster. It relaxes me.
Fabric from old banners becomes new aprons. Colours live twice in Harr.
Ask for a mend whenever a seam gives. Fixing is the best kind of making.

residents.name: Nadia Brightwick
residents.capabilities: Assembles street lamps, neon tubes and warm window lamps, and tunes each colour so every block has its own glow.
residents.limitations: Builds lamps and signs only; asks the site crew to hang them and the researchers for light-level readings.
barks: Pink for the market, cyan for the labs, violet for the school. Each district speaks in a colour.
A neon tube is a glass line you can bend with warm air and a steady breath. It never gets old.
The lantern path is lit by lamps I tested last week. Walk it after dark and tell me what you think.
I wear tinted glasses when I work. The glow can be bright, but it is always gentle once it is tuned.
Come by the workshop hall for a look at the bench. The sparks are tiny and the tea is hot.
Every lamp gets a number on its base, so a neighbour can tell the crew exactly which one needs care.

residents.name: Mirela Inkwell
residents.capabilities: Records urban plants, rooftop weather and air readings, and writes them into the library for all to read.
residents.limitations: Observes and writes only; leaves interpretation to a team of researchers and building to the site crew.
barks: Today's note: the rooftop garden is two degrees warmer than the avenue below. Tell me what you feel.
Weather is a conversation with the sky. I only write down what it says.
Please do not move the sensor cases at the research tower. They are small, polite and very accurate.
Moss, ferns and mint all have a story. I have written forty so far and I am slow.
I sit in the workshop hall at midday for the quiet. It smells of tea and lamp glass.
A notebook, a pen and a tablet. Between them I almost have everything. Almost.

residents.name: Dov Quillan
residents.capabilities: Studies optics, mirrors and night-sky data from the moon terrace and the observatory, and keeps the telescope lenses clean.
residents.limitations: Looks at the sky only; asks the site crew for platform work and the fabricators for custom lenses.
barks: The moon terrace has the darkest sky nearby. Come on a clear night and bring a jacket.
I breathe on a lens and polish it with a soft cloth. My dad did the same with his reading glasses.
Starlight is old. It left its star before the first tower of Harr went up.
The solar array gives me power for the telescope. A small thank you to the sun, every evening.
At the tram halt I check the platform clock. Good timing is half of astronomy.
If you see a long white trail across the sky, that is a plane or a satellite. I still wave.

residents.name: Oren Pagefold
residents.capabilities: Keeps the open archive: catalogues the library, keeps cross-indexes tidy and helps visitors find a page they need.
residents.limitations: Files and finds only; leaves research to the researchers and building to the site crew.
barks: The archive is open to everyone. Walk in, sit down and ask for any page, in any order.
I label every shelf in two colours so the city can find things even in the dim.
A well kept index is a map of everything we know. I enjoy drawing it.
The recycling garden sorts the paper for me. I still read every note before it goes.
Quiet please, but only a little. Learning is allowed to laugh now and then.
My favourite shelf is the one with the unfinished notes. That is where the next chapter starts.

residents.name: Wren Swiftpath
residents.capabilities: Runs messages, forecasts and research notes between the farm towers, the library and the plaza on foot and by light scooter.
residents.limitations: Carries news only; relies on the researchers for facts and on the hosts for the schedule.
barks: Message for the farm tower, forecast for the plaza and a note for the library. Busy and happy.
Running shoes, a reflective vest and a bag of notes. That is my whole uniform.
Cross at the signal and wave at the cameras. They wave back in light.
North cottage row is a good place for a breather. The benches are shaded and the lamps are soft.
I never take the same route twice in a row. It is the best way to meet new neighbours.
If you need a message carried, ask. I run past nearly everyone before lunch.

residents.name: Alder Roamfield
residents.capabilities: Walks the avenues and footbridges to check that lamps, rails and signs are in good order, and tells the runners about changes.
residents.limitations: Checks routes only; passes repair requests to the site crew and leaves lamp tuning to the fabricators.
barks: The footbridge by the guesthouse has a new handrail. Hold it and feel how smooth it is.
I count lamps as I walk. Tonight every one on the lantern path is glowing.
My thermos, my map and a spare battery. A good runner's checklist.
The vertical farm path is clear and dry. Mind the little puddles near the reflective lines.
If a sign looks odd, tell me. I will stop by on my next circuit and make a note.
I like the guesthouse step for a rest. Someone is always there to say good evening.

residents.name: Tamsin Wayfarer
residents.capabilities: Plans tram timetables, delivers pantry crates between the farm towers and the market, and tells newcomers which line goes where.
residents.limitations: Plans and delivers only; leaves cooking to the stalls and the tram tracks to the site crew.
barks: The next tram to the plaza is in six minutes. The one after is in twelve. Plenty of time for a bowl.
I keep the schedule in my head and on a screen, in case my head takes a night off.
Pantry crates ride on the bike carts. Apples first, lettuce second, gently always.
The amphitheatre stop is one of my favourites. The seats there catch the evening breeze.
A tram timetable is a promise. We keep it as best we can and say sorry kindly when we cannot.
Lost? Tell me where you are going and I will point you to the closest line.

residents.name: Lucia Lanternly
residents.capabilities: Welcomes visitors, opens the guesthouse, serves tea and shows newcomers the districts on the night map.
residents.limitations: Hosts and guides only; leaves cooking to the stalls and building to the site crew.
barks: Welcome to Harr. Tea is hot, the couches are soft and you can take as long as you like.
The night map on the wall shows every district. Find the one that sounds like you.
I wear a name badge and a warm cardigan. The badge says Lucia, the cardigan says relax.
Newcomers often ask where to begin. My answer is always the plaza and a bowl of noodles.
The guesthouse lamp stays on all night. If you need a quiet corner, come in.
A good host listens first. Tell me what you hope to find and I will think of a place.

residents.name: Ravi Hearthstone
residents.capabilities: Hosts the rooftop circle, keeps the city calendar and welcomes everyone who wants to read aloud or just listen.
residents.limitations: Hosts and keeps schedules only; relies on the researchers for content and on the runners for news.
barks: Rooftop circle starts on the half hour. Bring a page or bring a cup of tea, either is welcome.
The calendar is pinned in the library. Lantern Night is on Sundays at three, all are invited.
I read slowly so the wind does not carry the words away. The city leans in to listen.
Anyone may add a page. A single sentence counts, and so does a good question.
My jacket has a pocket for every cable and a pocket for snacks. Both are important.
When the circle ends, we stay a minute in silence. It is how the words settle.

residents.name: Odalys Evensong
residents.capabilities: Plays soft synth and flute on the roof at twilight, leads gentle sing-along rounds and helps organise Lantern Night.
residents.limitations: Plays and leads songs only; gets help from the site crew with stages and from the hosts with the schedule.
barks: At twilight I play on the sky walk. The cables hum along if the wind is right.
If you know a tune, hum it. The city is always ready for a new line.
My small speaker runs on the solar array. Every note is sunlight from earlier in the day.
Lantern Night begins with one song and ends with everyone. I am never alone on stage.
The second solar field catches the last light. I walk there when I need a new melody.
Sing as softly as you like. The rooftops are good at listening.

residents.name: Anselm Stonehand
residents.capabilities: Sets stair risers, levels plaza paving and builds retaining walls so the big stairs between the avenue levels are wide and gentle.
residents.limitations: Builds stairs and paving only; asks the researchers for slope data and the fabricators for handrail fittings.
barks: Wide stairs mean no one rushes. Take them slowly and enjoy the neon on each landing.
Every riser is the same height. A steady step is a kindness to tired legs.
The plaza paving is dark and glossy after rain. It looks like a second sky.
Market hall site is busy at dusk. Bring a friend and watch the next stage rise.
I keep a small level in my pocket. It tells me when I am right and when I am only hopeful.
At the observatory site the view is worth the climb. The stairs are mine, the view belongs to everyone.

residents.name: Briony Fieldwright
residents.capabilities: Trains climbing beans, peas and clover on the trellis walls of the vertical farm and keeps the soil bright and rich.
residents.limitations: Grows trellis crops only; leaves cranes to the site crew and recipes to the stalls.
barks: The bean wall on level five is full of flowers. They look like pink sparks against the glass.
Clover is a quiet friend. It feeds the soil while it feeds the bees.
At the orchard gate I wait for the first light. It turns the glass walls honey coloured.
Seedlings on tiny shelves, then bigger shelves, then the wall. It is a lot like a student's life.
Take a handful of peas on your way. They taste best still warm from the grow lamps.
I wear a green beanie and a long apron. The plants have never complained about my style.

residents.name: Cassian Quillmark
residents.capabilities: Analyses ground samples, river pebble layers and mineral content under the districts, and writes what he learns into the archive.
residents.limitations: Studies ground and minerals only; asks the site crew for samples and leaves construction choices to them.
barks: The ground beneath the research tower is firm and steady. That is good news for taller towers.
Each layer of pebbles tells how a river once ran where the avenue is now.
I label each sample bag with a date and a small drawing. It helps me remember the day.
At the solar array site the soil is dry and clean. A pleasant place for a quiet lunch.
Ask me about stones and I will talk too long. Please stop me with a cup of tea.
The vertical farm sits on bedrock, which is why the tower hardly moves in the wind.

residents.name: Delia Swiftpath
residents.capabilities: Runs dispatches along the northern avenues, carries archive updates to the farm towers and checks that the lamps are on.
residents.limitations: Carries news and checks routes only; relies on the hosts for the schedule and the fabricators for lamps.
barks: Dispatch from the archive: three new pages today. Please enjoy them.
Northern avenue is lovely at dusk. The windows turn gold and cyan, one after another.
I stop at the fountain every evening. The light there is soft enough for tired eyes.
A good runner takes breaks. Mine are at the transit hub and the archive steps.
Tell me what you want to know and I will bring the answer when I come back from the next run.
My shoes have reflective heels. If you see a flash on the avenue, that is me.

residents.name: Eamon Hearthstone
residents.capabilities: Looks after the seed bank, labels germination jars and coordinates seed swaps between the rooftop gardens and the farm towers.
residents.limitations: Keeps seeds and labels only; relies on the growers for planting and the researchers for lab notes.
barks: Every seed in the bank has a name, a date and a story. I love reading them aloud.
Swap day is on the sky walk. Bring a seed, take a seed, and tell us how it did.
Germination jars sit by the glass garden window. They love the morning light.
At the rooftop garden I plant the very first seeds of spring. It is my favourite hour.
I keep a notebook of the funniest labels. One jar simply says, we will see.
A seed is a promise with a lid. We open it when the time is right.

residents.name: Fable Loomwright
residents.capabilities: Braids baskets, bags and plant hangers from recycled fibre offcuts and helps the fabricators reuse leftover material.
residents.limitations: Weaves from offcuts only; asks the growers for fibre and the labs for custom fittings.
barks: This bag is braided from old banners. Look closely and you can still read a letter or two.
A basket should be light and strong. If it sings a little when you pick it up, it is right.
The rooftop garden hangers I made last week are already full of herbs.
I sit by the archive vault when I weave. The vault is quiet and the air is cool.
Bring me your torn bag and I will give it a second life. Mending is just weaving again.
The canal bridge is a good place to dry reeds. The breeze under the avenue is gentle.

residents.name: Galen Beamwright
residents.capabilities: Assembles laminated roof trusses, long beams and curved ribs, and sets bridge decks from engineered wood and steel.
residents.limitations: Builds beams and roofs only; asks the researchers for load numbers and the fabricators for fittings.
barks: A long beam needs six steady shoulders and one clear voice calling the lift.
From the sky bridge view you can see how our curved roofs echo the lights of the avenue.
I rub a little beeswax from the rooftop hive on the joints so they slide together smoothly.
Pause in the sparrow court and look up. Branches taught engineers about arches.
I measure twice with a steel tape and once with my hands. It is a habit.
At the moss wall I take a breath of cool, green air. It makes the afternoon easy.

residents.name: Hana Greenfurrow
residents.capabilities: Raises squash, pumpkin and bean vines on the balcony beds and companion-plants herbs to keep the soil lively.
residents.limitations: Grows balcony crops only; asks the site crew for rails and the researchers for soil results.
barks: Squash vines are climbing the balcony. If you pass by, you may need to duck a little.
Companion planting is neighbourliness for plants. Beans help corn, corn helps beans.
The sparrow court is where I eat lunch. The birds and I have an understanding.
I wear my hair in a scarf and my sleeves rolled. The vines tickle, but I do not mind.
On the moon terrace I water the night-blooming flowers. They open as soon as the sky clears.
At the transit interchange the breeze is strong. I tie my vines low and kind.

residents.name: Isolde Starwell
residents.capabilities: Maps old footpaths and new routes, draws district maps for the library and updates the tram diagrams.
residents.limitations: Draws maps only; checks distances with the runners and leaves construction to the site crew.
barks: The transit interchange has a new map on the wall. Find the star that says you are here.
Maps are friendly lies that get closer to the truth each time we redraw them.
Old footpaths became avenues, and avenues became bike lanes. I enjoy following the changes.
At the well site I sketch the plaza from the same bench every Friday.
The market hall has a bright new route sign. I drew the arrows myself.
My pencil case holds eleven colours. Cyan is my favourite for rivers and rails.

residents.name: Jarek Larkstep
residents.capabilities: Checks footbridges and stepping paths, carries instruments to the observatory and brings the library new field notes.
residents.limitations: Checks paths and carries things only; passes repair needs to the site crew.
barks: Footbridge check done. All railings feel solid and every lamp is glowing.
I carry the telescope case with both hands and a lot of care. It is lighter than it looks, thankfully.
Cottage Row is my favourite stop. The windows glow in warm orange after dark.
The pavilion lamps hum when the wind blows. I find that very comforting.
My backpack has a tiny first aid kit and a tinier umbrella. Both are optimistic.
Say hello at the annex if you see me. I always have time for a wave.

residents.name: Kalen Lanternson
residents.capabilities: Runs the shared tool library at the annex, keeps drivers, clamps and meters labelled and charged, and lends them to anyone who asks.
residents.limitations: Lends and tidies tools only; leaves repair jobs to the site crew and advice to the fabricators.
barks: Tools in the library are free to borrow. Bring them back charged and we will all be friends.
A clean tool is a happy tool. I wipe each one before it goes on the shelf.
Need a drill for a shelf? The annex has three and they all like quiet work.
The orchard gate has a small bench where I sit for a minute and watch the farm lights.
I wear a canvas apron with eleven pockets. Do not ask what is in them, because even I forget.
The research tower borrows our meters on Mondays. It is a good habit to share.

residents.name: Leena Kilnwood
residents.capabilities: Prints and fires tea cups, jugs and porous planters, and glazes them in the colours of the district lamps.
residents.limitations: Makes ceramics only; gets clay from the fabrication alley and asks the growers about planters.
barks: A tea cup should fit the hand, like a small warm handshake.
The glaze comes out cyan under the solar array lights. I did not plan it, but I like it.
Porous planters keep roots cool in summer. The vertical farm has a hundred of mine.
I wear a denim apron and listen to the radio. The cups come out better with a tune.
Visit the fountain at dusk and look at the cups on the ledge. They are free for a sip.
Fixing a chipped cup is easy. Bring it by the transit hub and I will see what I can do.

residents.name: Maren Mortar
residents.capabilities: Lays brick façades and permeable paving, mixes breathable mortar and repairs garden arches along the avenues.
residents.limitations: Lays brick and paving only; asks the researchers for materials data and the site crew for placement.
barks: Permeable paving lets rain pass through. The plaza stays dry and the soil stays happy.
Brick facades take the neon beautifully. Pink at night, red at sunrise.
I wear steel-capped boots and a bright jacket. Nobody has ever missed me on the avenue.
The sky walk site has a good rhythm. Four of us lay one stage before the lamps come on.
The glass garden arch is nearly done. Stop by and tell me if the curve feels kind.
Mortar likes patience. Quick hands make a mess, steady hands make a wall.

residents.name: Nestor Dewmeadow
residents.capabilities: Grafts pear and cherry saplings into planter walls, prunes trained espaliers and tends the blossoms along the rooftop paths.
residents.limitations: Grows fruit trees only; asks the site crew for rails and the researchers for pollinator counts.
barks: Pear blossom on the glass garden wall is open. Bees came before I could say hello.
An espalier is a tree taught to stand flat. It is very polite and very productive.
I trim in the early evening, when the lamps come on and the roof is quiet.
From the rooftop garden you can see the whole skyline. Bring a camera and a sweater.
The canal bridge has a lovely breeze under it, and my saplings enjoy it on warm days.
A scarf, a thermos and a pair of snips. Enough to make anyone happy.

residents.name: Oriel Inkwell
residents.capabilities: Logs cloud shapes and pressure on the roof station, sketches the evening sky and publishes the weather to the library.
residents.limitations: Records weather only; asks the researchers for analysis and the hosts to share the forecast.
barks: Pressure is rising slowly. Expect a clear evening and a sharp moon.
Clouds glow pink above the canal bridge tonight. I sketched them before they changed.
I sit on the sky bridge view with a flask of tea and a tablet. The sky does the rest.
A rooftop hive nearby makes a gentle hum. It is a good soundtrack for forecasting.
I wear a rain jacket in all seasons, just in case the sky has plans.
The moss wall changes colour a little before rain. I never get tired of watching it.

residents.name: Petra Wayfarer
residents.capabilities: Walks the park loop carrying material samples, delivers fabrication offcuts and brings back notes from the green belts.
residents.limitations: Carries samples and notes only; asks the fabricators about materials and the growers about plants.
barks: The park loop smells of damp leaves and tea. It is the best commute in Harr.
Sparrow court has a fresh set of nest boxes. Peek, but keep a respectful distance.
The moss wall bench is where I stop. The wall hums softly in the damp air.
Fabrication alley delivery is on my list. The ceramic offcuts clink like wind chimes.
From the moon terrace you can see the edge of the park lit by little blue lamps.
Boots, rain cape and a bag of samples. Not glamorous, but I love it.

residents.name: Quinlan Evenfall
residents.capabilities: Swaps and recharges lamp batteries, tests solar cells and keeps the moon terrace and the interchange lit through the night.
residents.limitations: Maintains batteries and lamps only; leaves wiring design to the fabricators and structure to the site crew.
barks: A fresh battery means a bright lamp. I carry a dozen in my satchel.
At the moon terrace the lamps are dim on purpose. The stars need the dark.
Interchange lamps are on a loop. When one fades, I swap it before anyone notices.
I wear a headlamp and a cap. I look a little like a tiny lighthouse.
Market hall is bright and loud, which is wonderful. Be sure to stop for tea.
A quiet shift ends when the last lamp reports green. I like that feeling.

residents.name: Renata Lathe
residents.capabilities: Turns handles and spindles on a precise lathe, knits warm scarves and builds small shelves and stools for homes and stalls.
residents.limitations: Makes small goods only; asks the site crew for large work and the fabricators for special fittings.
barks: Handles feel best when they have a little curve. A hand knows what a hand wants.
Scarf knit in magenta and cyan, for walking on windy avenues. Take one if you are cold.
The market hall stall has the stools I made. Sit down and try one.
Cottage row has a new shelf from my bench. It fits a plant and a book exactly.
At the observatory I leave a stool for tall researchers. Short ones may have two.
The pavilion needs a bench. I am sanding one tonight and humming.

residents.name: Soren Trusswell
residents.capabilities: Installs street lamp posts, runs low-voltage conduits and checks the solar-powered feeds for the avenues and the plaza.
residents.limitations: Installs lamp posts and conduits only; asks the lamp makers for fixtures and the researchers for load readings.
barks: A lamp post is a small tower. It stands in the rain so the walkers do not have to think about it.
The pavilion lamps are on a new loop. They should glow longer and softer.
I label every conduit with a colour and a number. A tidy cable is a safe cable.
Annex site is next. Bring a flask and watch the posts go up.
Orchard gate lights are done. They look like fireflies in a row.
At the research tower, lamps are on a schedule I enjoy. Dusk, midnight, dawn.

residents.name: Talia Oatley
residents.capabilities: Grows barley, oats and wheatgrass trays that become flour and noodles at the night market, and trims the grain rows in the farm tower.
residents.limitations: Grows grain only; leaves noodle making to the stalls and structure to the site crew.
barks: Oat trays by the research tower are green and tall. They bend like waves when the fan turns.
Barley becomes noodles, noodles become dinner. I find that very satisfying.
The solar array hums while I water. We are a small orchestra.
I wear a baseball cap and a long scarf. The fans in the grain room are playful.
Fountain light at dusk is my favourite break. The ripples look like grain in the wind.
Come see the trays. A hundred green stripes, all different heights.

residents.name: Ursa Lensfield
residents.capabilities: Studies moss walls and water filters, monitors air quality sensors and explains to visitors how the green walls keep the air fresh.
residents.limitations: Studies moss and filters only; leaves construction to the site crew and cooking to the stalls.
barks: Moss is small, patient and excellent at cleaning air. Be kind to it.
The fountain filter beds are clear this week. The sensors are all green.
I keep a magnifier on a string around my neck. Even the tiniest leaf has a design.
At the transit hub the air sensor shows fresh readings. A tram brings a little breeze each time.
Archive steps are my reading spot. A flask of tea, a sketchbook and a quiet tram.
Ask me why moss glows after rain. I love that question.

residents.name: Viola Satchel
residents.capabilities: Carries plant cuttings, seeds and jars of soil between the glass garden, the rooftop gardens and the farm towers.
residents.limitations: Carries cuttings and jars only; asks the growers for planting and the researchers for tests.
barks: A cutting in a damp cloth rides well on the sky walk. Wrap it and keep it cool.
I deliver to the glass garden every morning. The dome catches the first light first.
Rooftop garden to archive vault in nine minutes. My record, and the cuttings arrived happy.
My satchel smells like rosemary. I rarely mind.
On quiet evenings I rest at the sky walk and watch the trams slide past.
Need something carried? Wrap it carefully and I will do my best.

residents.name: Wendel Welcomeby
residents.capabilities: Keeps the guesthouse beds fresh, stocks the visitor shelves with blankets and maps and introduces newcomers to the districts.
residents.limitations: Welcomes and guides only; asks the cooks for meals and the site crew for repairs.
barks: Fresh blankets on every bed. They are folded the way my grandmother taught me.
The archive vault is a calm place to start. Ask the librarian for the first map.
From the canal bridge you can see the guesthouse sign glow. Walk toward the lilac light.
Visitors often leave notes in the guesthouse book. I read them all, and I smile.
The sky bridge view is a good first look at Harr. I recommend it.
The rooftop hive has a bench nearby. Sit, breathe and listen to the hum.

residents.name: Xanthe Threadgood
residents.capabilities: Prints and carves spoons, dippers and salad tongs from recycled wood-fibre offcuts for the night market stalls.
residents.limitations: Makes small utensils only; asks the labs for material and the stalls what they need.
barks: A spoon should sit in the hand like it grew there. I try a few until one feels right.
Rooftop hive honey dippers are my favourite. They never drip.
I sand utensils at the moss wall. The cool air keeps the dust down.
Sparrow court is where I carve in the afternoon. The birds critique quietly.
Fabrication alley has the best scraps. Every piece is a new idea.
If you need chopsticks, I have a bucket of them. Take as many as you like.

residents.name: Yorick Plumbline
residents.capabilities: Fits double-glazed windows, skylight vents and weather seals on towers and apartment blocks.
residents.limitations: Fits glass and seals only; asks the researchers for readings and the site crew for lifts.
barks: Double glazing keeps the neon glow soft indoors and the city hum outside.
A skylight vent breathes in the evening air. I check them with a feather and a smile.
I wipe each pane with a soft cloth before sealing. It feels like polishing a mirror.
At the moon terrace the windows are tinted to protect the night sky. A thoughtful touch.
The transit interchange has glass walls I installed in spring. Come and see them shine.
A good seal is silent. If you cannot hear it, I did my job.

residents.name: Zelda Brookfield
residents.capabilities: Grows spiral herb gardens, dries mint and chamomile and blends tea for the night market and the guesthouse.
residents.limitations: Grows and blends tea only; leaves structure to the site crew and stalls to the cooks.
barks: Spiral herb garden on level two: mint at the bottom, thyme at the top, and room for a visitor.
Dried chamomile smells like a sunny afternoon. I keep a jar by my bed.
At the well site the water is cool and the herbs are happy. A neighbour waves every morning.
Market hall tea is brewed fresh. If the pot is empty, I will make more.
Cottage Row has a window box of mint that never stops. I trim it, and the whole street smells nice.
A small cup of peppermint before a long shift is my secret. Now it is ours.

residents.name: Adair Folio
residents.capabilities: Plots star charts from the moon terrace, works out the dates of eclipses and teaches visitors to read the sky.
residents.limitations: Charts the sky only; asks the site crew for platform work and the fabricators for lenses.
barks: Tonight the moon is a bright sliver. Come to the observatory and we will find a planet beside it.
A star chart is a map you read with your neck tipped back. Stretch first.
I hold a red torch so my eyes stay ready for the dark. Gentle on everyone nearby.
The pavilion offers a little shelter from the wind. We bring flasks and blankets.
At the annex I keep copies of the charts. Take one and mark what you see.
At the orchard gate the sky is dark enough for the faint cluster. I wait there for the clear nights.

residents.name: Beatrix Roadwise
residents.capabilities: Runs the eastern avenue circuit, relays solar array readings to the library and brings the farm tower news to the plaza.
residents.limitations: Carries readings and news only; asks the researchers for explanation and the fabricators for repairs.
barks: East avenue is quiet and lit in violet. A lovely loop for a short run.
Solar readings are up today. The array is soaking up all the bright sky it can.
I keep my route card in my sleeve. It says go gently, greet everybody.
Farm tower news: new cherry tomatoes, tall basil, a surprise pumpkin.
Research tower elevator is quiet and quick. A pleasant ride up and down.
Please wave when you see me. It makes the miles lighter.

content.title: Meet five villagers
content.short: Stand beside five neighbours around the plaza, the workshop hall and the farm tower.
content.purpose: Knowing your neighbours is the first step to working with them.
content.how: Walk up to the people around the plaza, the workshop hall and the farm tower and stand beside them for a moment.

content.title: Share a bowl at the night market
content.short: Whisper me: take apple. The market pantry is free for everyone.
content.purpose: The market pantry is free for everyone; a shared bowl is the simplest kind of welcome.
content.how: Whisper Selene: take apple. The night market pantry is free for everyone.

content.title: Find a viewpoint for the library
content.short: Whisper me: library, then walk to {place} and stay a few seconds.
content.purpose: Every viewpoint recorded is a page the whole city can read.
content.how: Whisper Selene: library, then walk to {place} and stay a few seconds.

content.title: Lend a hand to the site crew
content.short: Whisper me: works, then stand with the site crew at a site that waits for a crew.
content.purpose: A stage is built only while a crew stands at the site; a visitor can be part of that crew.
content.how: Whisper Selene: works. When a stage waits for a crew, stand with the site crew at its site until it is built; the city records who helped.

content.title: Take the Quiet Survey with Lyra
content.short: Stand beside Lyra at the library and she will walk the survey with you.
content.purpose: Walking a survey with a researcher is how a practice becomes a record.
content.how: Stand beside Lyra at the library; she will walk the field survey with you along the farm rows. It is a practice and awards nothing.

content.title: Keep your progress in NemoWorld
content.short: Whisper Lyra: link my account. She sends a private code.
content.purpose: A linked character lets the city remember what you did, not only what you said.
content.how: Whisper Lyra: link my account. She sends a private code to enter on the NemoWorld link page.

content.title: Add three pages to the library
content.short: Visit viewpoints from the library list; three pages in all.
content.purpose: Every find adds insight for the whole city and brings the next technology closer.
content.how: Whisper Selene: library for hints. Three different viewpoints is enough.

content.title: Walk with a neighbour to a place
content.short: Stand beside a neighbour inside a landmark for a few seconds.
content.purpose: The city grows by doing things together, not by watching from the kerb.
content.how: Stand beside a resident inside a landmark for a few seconds; the game records that you were there together.

content.title: Walk five rooftops
content.short: Visit five viewpoints from the library list.
content.purpose: The skyline looks different from every roof; five viewpoints give you the shape of the whole district.
content.how: Whisper Selene: library for the list. Stand a few seconds at each of five different viewpoints, such as {place}.

content.title: See every viewpoint
content.short: Find all ten viewpoints and complete the rooftop catalogue.
content.purpose: A complete catalogue is a gift to every researcher who comes after you.
content.how: Whisper Selene: library. Visit all ten viewpoints, from the rooftop garden to the moon terrace, and the catalogue is whole.

content.title: Become a night market regular
content.short: Whisper me: take apple, three times on three visits.
content.purpose: There is enough for everyone, and coming back for a second and third bowl is welcome.
content.how: Whisper Selene: take apple, then come back on another visit for more. The stalls are restocked by the vertical farms.

content.title: Stand with two site crews
content.short: Whisper me: works, then stand with the crews at two different sites.
content.purpose: Every tower, bridge and home is raised by different crews; seeing two shows how the city fits together.
content.how: Whisper Selene: works. Stand with the site crew at one site until a stage is built, then do the same at a second site.

content.title: Meet ten neighbours
content.short: Stand beside ten different people across the districts.
content.purpose: A city is the people who keep each other company. Ten greetings is a good start.
content.how: Walk the plaza, the workshop hall, the farm tower and the archive, and stand beside ten different residents for a moment each.

content.title: Keep a neighbour company
content.short: Stand beside a neighbour at three different places.
content.purpose: Shared moments are how newcomers become neighbours.
content.how: Stand beside a resident inside three different landmarks for a few seconds each; the game records that you were there together.

content.title: A night out in Harr
content.short: Meet neighbours, find viewpoints, share a bowl and keep someone company.
content.purpose: A good night in the city has a little of everything: people, views, food and company.
content.how: Meet three residents, visit two viewpoints, take one bowl from the pantry and stand beside a neighbour at a landmark, in any order.

content.title: Keep the open archive
content.short: Link your account, take the survey and record five viewpoints.
content.purpose: An open archive only stays useful when people add to it and sign their pages.
content.how: Link your account with Lyra, walk the Quiet Survey with her and record five viewpoints, in any order; your pages stay yours in the archive.

content.title: A page for the next reader
content.blurb: Write down what you learn so the next person starts further on.

steps.label: Stand a few seconds at a viewpoint from the library.
Greet two neighbours and ask what they are working on.
Add two more viewpoints to the library.

content.title: Insight for everyone
content.blurb: Every find teaches the whole city something new.

steps.label: Find two viewpoints; each one adds insight for all.
Stand at a building site with neighbours and watch the work.
Ask four different neighbours what the city is learning.
Bring the library to five viewpoints in all.

content.title: Many hands
content.blurb: Big works need a crew. Come and stand with it.

steps.label: Meet three site crew, fabricators or neighbours near the plaza.
Stand with a crew at a building site.
Visit a second site and stand with its crew too.

content.title: A warm welcome
content.blurb: Harr grows when newcomers feel at home.

steps.label: Introduce yourself to five neighbours.
Share a first bowl from the free night market pantry.
Keep your progress in NemoWorld by linking your account with Lyra.
Join neighbours at a place in the city.

content.title: Up to the rooftops
content.blurb: The city is full of views worth finding.

steps.label: Find your first viewpoint.
Find four viewpoints in all, a few steps from the plaza each.
Seven viewpoints make a studious skyline.

content.title: Share the table
content.blurb: There is enough. The night market is open to everyone.

steps.label: Take something from the pantry; ask Selene for an apple.
Tell three neighbours what you ate; growers love to hear.
Come back for a second helping on another visit.

content.title: The catalogue keeper
content.blurb: A good catalogue is a gift to every researcher after you.

steps.label: Record five viewpoints for the library.
Link your account so your name stays on your pages.
Compare notes with six different neighbours.
Record eight viewpoints in all.

content.title: Field season
content.blurb: Careful looking, again and again, is how research grows.

steps.label: Visit three viewpoints and read their field notes.
Stand with neighbours at two different places.
Extend the survey to six viewpoints.
Share what you found with eight neighbours.

content.title: Good neighbours
content.blurb: A city is the people who keep each other company.

steps.label: Say hello to four neighbours.
Stand with others at a shared place.
Share a snack from the pantry beside a neighbour.
Visit three shared places in the city.

content.title: Rising Harr
content.blurb: Harr is never finished. Come and see what is rising.

steps.label: Ask two site crew what is going up next.
Find two viewpoints where the next towers could rise.
Stand at two building sites.
Link your account so the city remembers you.

content.title: The whole skyline
content.blurb: Ten viewpoints, ten pages, one complete catalogue.

steps.label: Find three viewpoints.
Find six viewpoints.
Complete the catalogue: all ten viewpoints.

content.title: Farm tower and noodle stall
content.blurb: What the farm towers grow, the city shares.

steps.label: Share two helpings from the pantry.
Thank six neighbours for the farms, tools and lamps.
Share a third helping with a friend.
Link your account so your meals are kept in your story.

techs.name: Field notes
techs.text: Researchers log every find from the rooftops and avenues, so each page in the Library is richer.

techs.name: Grow-light science
techs.text: Growers learn which light, water and nutrients suit which crops in a stacked indoor farm.

techs.name: Clean water mains
techs.text: The plaza well is joined to a clean main; every night market kitchen has water at hand.

techs.name: Neighbourhood grid power
techs.text: Rooftop panels and shared batteries keep the lamps lit all night. Next stop: a glowing, walkable avenue.

techs.name: Nutrient loops
techs.text: Nothing is wasted: kitchen scraps and tank water return to the growing rooms as feed.

techs.name: Glass towers
techs.text: Clear structural glass makes bright atriums, observatory domes and tall towers possible.

techs.name: Vertical farms
techs.text: Crops grown in stacked, light-filled floors feed more people from less ground.

techs.name: City mapping
techs.text: Every discovered viewpoint is drawn on a shared city map that anyone can read.

techs.name: Open data archive
techs.text: All findings are kept in a public data archive that other cities can learn from.

techs.name: Maglev sky transit
techs.text: Quiet magnetic-levitation trains and landing decks join Harr to the wider world.

techs.name: Rooftop rain capture
techs.text: Tiled roof basins catch the rain, keeping market kitchens flowing even through dry spells.

techs.name: Rooftop gardens
techs.text: Mint, chamomile and herb beds on the roofs give tea for the night market and a quiet place to think.

techs.name: Steel and glass framing
techs.text: Light modular frames let site crews raise wide halls and tall towers with fewer parts.

techs.name: Neon sign craft
techs.text: Fabricators bend glowing tubes in pink, cyan and violet, so every district has its own colour at night.

techs.name: Cold-chain storage
techs.text: Chilled vaults under the market keep fruit and noodles fresh for weeks without waste.

techs.name: Solar street paving
techs.text: Pavement tiles gather daylight and glow softly along the avenues through the night.

techs.name: Hydroponic districts
techs.text: Whole blocks of closed-loop water tanks grow greens with no run-off.

techs.name: Public wifi
techs.text: Free city-wide wireless lets anyone read the archive from a bench, a bridge or a rooftop.

techs.name: Mushroom halls
techs.text: Dark, cool halls under the towers grow edible mushrooms that refill the market shelves.

techs.name: Clean transit grid
techs.text: Electric trams, shared bikes and quiet buses connect every district without a single exhaust pipe.

techs.name: Urban ecology surveys
techs.text: Systematic notes on pollinators, moss walls and bird routes across the rooftops.

techs.name: Fabrication labs
techs.text: Open labs with precise printers and laser cutters make durable lamps, panels and pantry containers.

techs.name: City seed bank
techs.text: Carefully catalogued seeds from many places safeguard the city's food diversity for decades.

techs.name: Sky bridge network
techs.text: Glass-floored bridges let neighbours stroll between towers high above the avenues.

techs.name: Observatory optics
techs.text: Precisely ground mirrors reveal fine detail on the moon and distant stars from the roof terrace.

techs.name: Night-sky spectroscopy
techs.text: Splitting starlight shows what far-off suns are made of, right from the observatory dome.

techs.name: Bio-composite materials
techs.text: Light, strong panels grown from plant fibre and mycelium replace heavy metal fittings in new builds.

techs.name: District heating loops
techs.text: Warm water loops from the data halls heat the growing rooms in winter and cool the apartments in summer.

techs.name: The open city lexicon
techs.text: A shared open encyclopaedia joins plant, building and star terms for every researcher in the city.

techs.name: The night market
techs.text: With clean power, shared food and open learning in place, the whole city gathers under lanterns to share a meal.
